text: #383, in place of D-0271 after #390's review: a file marked # +nagini may import nothing its package holds, marked or not, since a proved core can rest only on itself, the standard library and the modules Nagini models. The pinned Nagini takes an imported module's contracts without proving its bodies, and the one local import D-0271 let through, a bare import of a sibling marked core, binds where the code runs to whatever the launcher's path finds first, the project root before the package: with a plain root helper.py, the real gate passed and counted a function proved that broke its postcondition when it ran. So before Nagini runs, the gate reads every import a marked file holds, wherever it stands, in a function, a branch or a try as at the top, and refuses each of what the package holds, as a module, a stub, a directory, a stub package or a compiled module, a test or a marked file among them, as well as a relative import and the package by its own name. Imports of the standard library, of nagini_contracts and of what the package doesn't hold are unaffected, and a top-level name the standard library or nagini_contracts provides is theirs whatever the package holds, since that is the module Python loads. A refusal fails the code check with an error on each line it refuses, the refused file's functions are named as ones Nagini never saw, and a marked file the core would import is proved alone. Nagini proves each marked file in a directory holding only that file, with the bytes the gate read, so it reads no module of the project. An in-place proof can't reach a sibling's contracts this way: its verifier input binds every name beyond its module only to a trusted contract's abstraction in a module the gate writes, in a directory holding only the input, so what an in-place proof may do is unchanged. Today's three cores import nothing of their package, and pass.
